lab_title: AR Lab: Structural Anatomy of the Heart & Dual-Loop Blood Pathway
top_level_objectives: Identify the four cardiac chambers and explain their roles in blood flow.
Identify the four major heart valves and describe how they prevent backflow.
Trace the major vessels entering and leaving the heart (SVC/IVC, pulmonary arteries/veins, aorta).
Follow the dual-loop circulation path: systemic → right heart → lungs → left heart → systemic.
Relate ventricular wall thickness to functional workload (right vs. left ventricular pumping demands).
Explain the flow direction through valves during the cardiac cycle using a sequential tracing approach.

scenes.brief_purpose: Help students establish spatial orientation to the heart model and recognize major anatomical landmarks.
key_visuals: A life-sized 3D heart model anchored in front of the student with anterior/inferior orientation cues
On-screen labels for left vs right side of the heart (student-facing convention)
Subtle highlighting of the atrial region vs ventricular region
student_actions: Rotate the heart (or reorient the view) to confirm which side is labeled left vs right.
Locate and tap hotspots to bring up brief prompts identifying “atria” and “ventricles.”
Answer a quick check: “Which chamber region would receive blood returning from the body?”

scenes.brief_purpose: Build competency in distinguishing right atrium, right ventricle, left atrium, and left ventricle on a 3D representation.
key_visuals: Sequential highlighting of each chamber in anatomical order (RA → RV → LA → LV)
Visual thickness cues: myocardium shading stronger in left ventricle
Callouts near septum and chamber walls to aid orientation
student_actions: Select each chamber hotspot when it appears and confirm the correct name.
Compare right vs left ventricle wall thickness by toggling a “thickness overlay” (prompted by the scene).
Record a brief statement: “Why do you think the left ventricle is thicker?”

scenes.brief_purpose: Enable students to identify tricuspid, pulmonary, mitral/bicuspid, and aortic valves and understand their directional control.
key_visuals: Color-coded valve rings that appear at correct anatomical positions
Valve motion hint (e.g., pulsing “open/closed” states synchronized to a simple animation)
Arrows indicating normal forward flow through each valve
student_actions: Trace the forward path across valves by tapping each valve when highlighted (tricuspid → pulmonary → mitral → aortic).
Indicate where backflow would occur if a valve failed by dragging a “backflow” arrow (no need for detailed mechanics, just correct conceptual location).
Answer: “Which valve sits between the left atrium and left ventricle?”

scenes.brief_purpose: Connect chambers to the major vessels entering/leaving the heart: SVC, IVC, pulmonary arteries, pulmonary veins, and aorta.
key_visuals: Animated vessel streamlines: inflow streams converge toward the right atrium; outflow streams exit from ventricles
Distinct color channels for systemic venous return (SVC/IVC), pulmonary flow, and systemic arterial outflow (aorta)
Label cards for each vessel with brief vessel-type descriptor (vein/artery)
student_actions: Match each vessel label to its place on the 3D model by tapping corresponding hotspots.
Follow one color channel end-to-end: from SVC/IVC into the heart and from the aorta back out.
Make a quick prediction: “Which vessel brings oxygenated blood back to the heart?”

scenes.brief_purpose: Teach the complete dual-loop circulation sequence through the chambers, valves, and major vessels.
key_visuals: A step-by-step animated tracer (e.g., oxygen state changes from deoxygenated to oxygenated)
Sequential highlighting of structures as the tracer passes (chambers then valves then vessels)
Two-loop schematic overlay that links the on-model path to the systemic/pulmonary loops
student_actions: Start the tracer at the body return and follow it through the right heart to the lungs.
Continue the tracer as oxygenated blood returns to the left atrium and exits via the aortic pathway.
At each loop transition, confirm the chamber where the tracer is currently located (prompted by the scene).

scenes.scene_name: Function Connection: Why Left Ventricle Is the Workhorse
scenes.brief_purpose: Solidify the relationship between anatomy (wall thickness) and physiology (pump resistance/workload) in the dual-loop model.
key_visuals: A comparison overlay highlighting right vs left ventricular wall thickness
Pressure/workload bars that increase for systemic outflow relative to pulmonary outflow (qualitative, not numerical)
Animation showing the left ventricle driving flow into the entire systemic network vs the right ventricle driving flow to lungs only
student_actions: Toggle a “workload comparison” view and describe the qualitative difference in pumping demand.
Choose the best explanation for left ventricle thickness by selecting from provided statements.
Explain (in your own words) how valves ensure one-way flow during this pumping process.
